Preprint — arXiv:2505.07473v1 (cs.AI); no venue stated
Industry: ByteDance (all four authors)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark Web-Bench (50 web projects x 20 sequentially dependent tasks with Playwright E2E tests) and comparison of 40 LLMs through the authors' Web-Agent

No SDD approach. Fixed benchmark agent: Web-Agent (authors' prompt-building / LLM-request / file-extraction module inspired by Continue; version Not stated); custom agents can be plugged in via HTTP-Agent. Models: 40 LLMs (Table 9), e.g. claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219(-thinking), gpt-4.1, deepseek-r1, gemini-2.5-pro, doubao-pro-1.5-thinking

Per project: tasks.jsonl (20 task descriptions, sequentially dependent), src-init/ (initial code), src/ (final reference solution), test/ (init.spec.js and task-1..task-20.spec.js E2E cases). Agent prompt: system prompt (code-block rules), task description, current files, error messages (truncated to the context length)

Evaluator: get initial code -> iterate task-1..task-20: call agent (build prompt, request LLM, extract files) -> rewrite files -> init env -> build -> Playwright E2E test -> on failure retry once with error context (second failure ends the evaluation) -> report
None during runs. Project calibration during construction: engineers fix ambiguous task descriptions and too strict / not rigorous tests, using runs with claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
N/A (no SDD approach); single-pass LLM code generation per task inside a sequential project, via a minimal agent

Automatic: Web-Bench evaluator in Docker runs Playwright E2E tests after each task and computes Pass@1/Pass@2

Criterion: task passed = all E2E tests of the task pass; no configuration-level threshold. Best-of-5 sampling. Model settings by vendor (Table 2): context 50,000 (Anthropic) or 10,000 (others), max tokens 4,096-8,192, temperature 0-1 or default. For every configuration: quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: N/A (not measured)

Project/tasks: Web-Bench 50 projects x 20 tasks. Configurations: 40 LLMs under the same Web-Agent; per-framework subsets (React/Vue/Angular/Svelte; Redux/Mobx/Zustand/Jotai; Next/Nuxt/Express/Fastify; databases) compared for 6 models (Pass@2). Baseline: none. Held constant: agent, system prompt, tasks, tests, evaluator; model parameters vary by vendor (context length, max tokens, temperature). Acceptance tests: Playwright E2E tests per task. Repetitions: Best-of-5 sampling. Human intervention: none; one automatic retry with error context

claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-thinking best (Pass@1 25.11%, Pass@2 35.33%); Claude series highest, then GPT, Doubao, DeepSeek. Closed models average Pass@1 15.08% / Pass@2 20.79% vs open 10.73% / 14.84%. Newer or larger models and thinking mode generally better. Framework-level: e.g. React and Zustand easier, Angular harder; Express better than Next.js. No significance tests

Distinguished 40 models with an unsaturated SOTA (25.1% Pass@1 vs 65.4% SWE-bench Verified). Repeatability: Best-of-5 sampling, no variance; Docker-based evaluator, data on GitHub and Hugging Face. Limitations of the comparison not discussed (vendor-specific parameters, single minimal agent)

Limitations: many standards and frameworks not yet covered (workload); only code-generation accuracy measured, not aesthetics or code quality (screenshot function exists for future metrics); a Lite version planned because of evaluation cost. Gap / claim: LLMs need optimisation tailored to standards and frameworks (standards-aware training, framework-specific adaptation), presented as an intuition and future work

Possible inconsistency: Table 9 percentages are all multiples of 1/920 (e.g. 25.11% = 231/920, 6.52% = 60/920), suggesting 920 tasks (46 projects) were scored, not 50 x 20 = 1,000 (check). 'Pass@1' is reported with Best-of-5 sampling (p. 5), which differs from the usual single-sample Pass@1; Error@1 not defined. Appendix C.2 (p. 26) says benchmark projects are 'mostly single files, a few single-digit files', which conflicts with Table 1 (reference solutions average 23.4 files, max 76). Abstract calls the lower SOTA 'significantly lower (better)'. Table 2 temperatures per vendor are hard to align from the text. Projects calibrated with claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 (Appendix D), which may favour Claude models. Doubao is a ByteDance model evaluated by ByteDance authors. Replication package: https://github.com/bytedance/web-bench and Hugging Face dataset bytedance-research/WebBench. No pre-registration. Programming language: JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, CSS
